newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreign direct investment in Japan soars to record.
newsitem.headline: Foreign direct investment in Japan soars to record.

text.p: Direct investment by foreign companies in Japan rose to its highest level ever in the past business year, the government said on Friday.
The Finance Ministry said the value of investment by foreign companies jumped to 770 billion yen ($6.63 billion) in the 1996/97 year ended March 31.
The previous record was 590 billion yen ($5.08 billion) set in 1991.
Meanwhile, investment abroad by Japanese firms increased for the third year in a row, rising nine percent to 5.41 trillion yen ($46.6 billion) as manufacturers continued to shift facilities offshore.
A ministry official said while the number of cases of investment by foreign firms in Japan actually decreased, the amount of money involved had climbed.

High-profile investments included Ford Motor's move to raise its stake in Mazda Motor Corp to one-third and purchases of blue-chip properties in Japan by Singapore's Alderney Investment Pte Ltd and Hong Kong's Pacific Century Group.
For domestic firms, the United States remained the most attractive country, claiming nearly half of all of Japanese investment.
But China was knocked off its second place perch by Britain, as investment in the former fell 35 percent after tax incentives for foreign companies ended last year.

Direct investment in Vietnam and India nearly doubled although the amounts were still comparatively small at 36 billion yen ($310 million) and 25 billion yen ($215 million) respectively. Investment in Indonesia also rose sharply, up by 76 percent to 272 billion yen ($2.34 billion).
